newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new heights but falls may await.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new heights but falls may await.

text.p: Danish share prices closed on a record high for the third consecutive trading day on Tuesday, but dealers said that the market could turn edgy for the next few days, with much depending on Wall Street's performance and Friday's U.S. employment data.
"There could therefore be some profit-taking, but it shouldn't have too much effect because the underlying sentiment is good," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained a healthy 1.06 point to close at 138.72 in overall bourse turnover of 1.742 billion crowns.
Its March future stayed untraded at Monday's closing 138.75.

Shipping and energy group A.P.Moeller continued to benefit from rising oil prices. Its D/S Svendborg share rose two percent to 235,000 crowns and sister D/S 1912 grew 2.5 percent to 164,000. Dealers expected the shares to continue rising.
Cement and engineering group FLS, which earlier announced a 70 million crown Guatemalan order, climbed 21 crowns to 775.
Copenhagen Airports gained 15 crowns to 640 crowns and GN Store Nord picked up 10 crowns, to close at 600.
Among the losers were ISS, down two crowns to 152, Den Danske Bank, down 5.5 crowns to 476 and Carlsberg, down four to 398 crowns.
